title: AERO9500 Final Report (Part 2) — Space Mission Design
overview: Design a preliminary space mission that benefits Australia and report its mission concept and space-segment design. Apply course knowledge to explain the spacecraft, launch, orbit, communications, operations and end-of-life plan, using mission-design software and, where useful, hand calculations.
deliverables: A concise technical report as a single PDF, including relevant screenshots and all relevant STK or PIGI project files (in the report or an appendix).

format.length: Maximum 20 pages for the report core; title page, contents, references and similar front matter are excluded.
format.structure: Executive summary; Introduction (mission overview and rationale); Main body (space-segment design, including launch, orbit, ground stations, coverage, mission operations and end-of-life); Conclusion; Bibliography.
format.other: Use a clear, logical engineering-report style with correct grammar and spelling. Fully label figures and tables with numbers, titles and references where needed. Cite and reference all material not originating with you; Wikipedia is not an acceptable source.

requirements.text: Define the primary mission and explain how it benefits Australia; keep the mission concept simple.
Specify whether the mission uses one or multiple spacecraft.
Identify the users, including the operator and customers.
Specify the launch site and launch vehicle.
Describe the orbit, including its type, characteristics and orbital elements.
State whether orbital manoeuvres are required and describe them as relevant.
Identify the ground-control facilities and state how often the spacecraft can communicate with ground control.
Specify the mission duration and end-of-life plan.
Use mission-design software of your choice (STK or PIGI are suggested); contact the course representative before using other software. Supplement the design with hand calculations where useful.
